protocol.selection: lowest combined validation objective; held-out task-family and fresh-seed rows not used for checkpoint selection

inverse_diagnostic.source: original 124-train-row archive, not the expanded archive
inverse_diagnostic.input: observed before/after screen features to predict normalized click coordinates
inverse_diagnostic.action_type_baseline: all selected rows are clicks, so 100% action-type accuracy is uninformative

finding: General pointer-affordance extraction adds four previously missed task families. More varied training lowers pixel error but does not produce robust action grounding: the default model still prefers paired wrong clicks, and the pairwise model's positive fresh-seed mean advantage is only 0.000001889 weighted MSE. Observed after-screens modestly improve inverse localization; resolution alone does not solve it.
limitations: MiniWoB selected first-click pairs are not representative real desktop trajectories or multi-step task success.
Additional task families and the original held-out families were inspected during prior exploratory work; this is not an untouched preregistered benchmark.
The published state-transition pretraining recipe uses substantially larger data and a multimodal backbone; its results cannot be attributed to this small grayscale model.
No research weight is loaded by the live predictor or authorized to gate actions; no Jev parity, independent safety, or real desktop transfer is established.
